sourceEtymology.note: DEDR 1163 lists Kannada kaṇame/kaṇave/kaṇime/kaṇive for a narrow pass or gap between mountains, Tamil kaṇavāy for a mountain pass or ravine, and Tulu kaṇime for a defile or pass. No Proto-Dravidian reconstruction is supplied in this entry. The modern Kannada gloss ‘valley’ is broader; use the pass/ravine sense where precision matters.

editorial.note: The Kannada form ಕಣಿವೆ is historically attested in the Dravidian comparative record (DEDR 1163). Its older attested sense is a narrow mountain pass/gap or ravine; the broader modern ‘valley’ gloss should not be treated as identical in every context. Tamil and Tulu comparanda are recorded; no Proto-Dravidian reconstruction is supplied by this entry. Contributor-supplied alternatives remain subject to separate semantic review.
